description: Mortgage prequalification marketing rules: Regulation N (MAP Rule) prohibitions, Reg Z 1026.24 mortgage-specific provisions, NMLS/state display requirements.

parameters.no_condition: prohibited regardless of offer flags — mortgage prequal marketing may never claim or imply approval likelihood beyond 'prequalified' with qualifiers

rules.explanation: Reg N 12 CFR 1014.3(q) prohibits misrepresenting the likelihood of mortgage approval. Prequalification is not approval; 'pre-approved' badges/headlines on mortgage prequal placements are banned outright in this rulebook (offer matrix badge_designation_allowed is always 'prequalified' for mortgage).

Reg N 12 CFR 1014.3 prohibits misrepresenting whether a rate is fixed or adjustable; Reg Z 1026.24(i)(1) separately bans advertising a variable dwelling-secured rate as 'fixed'. Any 'fixed' language on a placement referencing an ARM offer cell is a critical violation.

parameters.disposition: flag_for_verification — permitted only when the offer is genuinely a government-program loan and no affiliation with a government agency is implied

rules.explanation: Reg N 12 CFR 1014.3(k)-(l) prohibits misrepresenting government affiliation or that a product is endorsed by/part of a government program. Government-program vocabulary is flagged for verification against the actual offer.

Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24(f): first-lien payment advertisements must state that the payment excludes taxes and insurance and that the actual obligation will be higher. Any monthly-payment figure on mortgage creative requires the taxes-and-insurance disclosure; Reg N 1014.3(f) separately bans payment misrepresentation.

SAFE Act-derived state rules (e.g. Virginia 10VAC5-160-60) require the company NMLS unique identifier on mortgage advertising, websites, and social profiles. Every mortgage creative must display the NMLS ID.

parameters.equal_prominence: when both an interest rate and an APR are shown, each with equal prominence and close proximity; rate may not be more conspicuous than APR

rules.explanation: Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24(b)-(c),(f): mortgage rate ads must state rates as APR (labeled); where a simple interest rate also appears it must sit with the APR at equal-or-lesser prominence.

Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24(i)(5) prohibits advertising claims that a dwelling-secured product will 'eliminate debt' or similar debt-elimination framing (a refinance restructures debt, it does not eliminate it); Reg N 1014.3(m) bans the equivalent misrepresentation of debt elimination.

parameters.staleness_note: mortgage cells carry ~3-day effective windows because pricing reprices daily; expired windows are automatic truthfulness failures

rules.explanation: Advertised mortgage rates/APRs must match the current offer-matrix window. Because mortgage pricing reprices ~daily, the effective_end check is the primary staleness control (the Amerisave third-party rate-table fact pattern).

parameters.scope: for-profit lender marketing may not describe itself or its staff as counselors

rules.explanation: Reg Z 12 CFR 1026.24(i)(6) prohibits a for-profit mortgage creditor from using the term 'counselor' to refer to itself or its employees in advertising.

parameters.judge_focus: Is the prequalification framing honest about what it is? Look for: 'prequalified' presented with the weight of an approval, missing or buried 'this is not a loan approval' qualifiers (some states require it at >=14pt bold), rate-lock implications, and whether the CTA implies certainty a prequal cannot deliver.

rules.explanation: Reg N 1014.3(q) net-impression zone: even without banned phrases, a prequal placement can imply approval certainty through design and framing. The judge assesses whether qualifiers adequately counter the overall impression.
